server_yaml_candidate.bandwidth_limits: Preserve current omitted/empty up and down so MaxTx=MaxRx=0. Preserve existing disableLossCompensation value.

units.yaml_bandwidth: Mbps is decimal megabits per second, lowercase b.

negotiation: Mihomo up becomes ClientOptions.SendBPS; down becomes ReceiveBPS.
Official server with IgnoreClientBandwidth=false and received Rx>0 selects Brutal for its sending/download side. MaxTx>0 can cap the negotiated value; with MaxTx=0 the requested value remains.
Official server replies Rx=server MaxRx and RxAuto=IgnoreClientBandwidth.
With Rx=0 and RxAuto=false, sing-quic uses configured client SendBPS. Positive SendBPS selects Brutal upload; zero selects the Mihomo BBR callback.
Current production profile omits both up and down, so fresh active connections remain BBR client and server even during the temporary server ignoreClientBandwidth=false setting.
Controllers are selected at authentication of a new QUIC connection. Existing connections do not renegotiate.

controller_verification.official_server_log: client connected includes tx in bytes per second
controller_verification.download_only_variant: Set down=50 Mbps and omit up to change only server/download controller while retaining client BBR.

interpretation_limit: Brutal requests a sender rate and compensates for estimated loss; the requested rate is not guaranteed application throughput. A bounded paired trial must measure actual transferred payload, elapsed time, failure rate, and restore the original server flag if benefit is absent.
